growth_problem: Qualified pipeline is leaking most at the webinar handoff: webinars bring the most leads but sales accepts very few of them. Paid search economics and the mobile demo form are smaller, separate leaks.

hypotheses.title: Webinar leads are learners, not buyers
hypotheses.observed_problem: Webinar leads become MQLs readily but sales rejects most of them.
hypotheses.causal_explanation: The MQL rules reward webinar attendance, so contacts without budget, authority, or an active project reach sales.
hypotheses.intervention: Add buying-intent questions to registration and require an intent signal before MQL.
hypotheses.expected_behavior_change: Fewer but better webinar MQLs; sales accepts a much larger share.
hypotheses.expected_business_outcome: More SQLs per sales hour and steady webinar-sourced pipeline.

supporting.claim: Webinar MQL to SQL conversion is far below other sources on large volume.
Most webinar rejections cite budget, authority, or student status.
Webinars convert leads to MQL better than any source but fail downstream.
Webinars are the largest lead source with the lowest lead-to-win rate.
Webinar attendees describe learning or research with no project or budget.

missing: How the MQL score weights webinar attendance.
Whether rejected webinar contacts convert later through nurture.

hypotheses.title: Unclear pricing is losing paid search evaluators
hypotheses.observed_problem: Paid search visitors exit the pricing page far more often than other traffic, fewer of them click through to a demo, and paid search acquisition cost has climbed.
hypotheses.affected_audience: Paid search evaluators, mostly small businesses, at the pricing step
hypotheses.causal_explanation: Evaluators cannot tell what each plan includes or what they would pay, so high-intent search visitors leave instead of requesting a demo.
hypotheses.intervention: A clearer plan comparison with explicit inclusions, usage limits, and an estimate of total cost.
hypotheses.expected_behavior_change: Lower pricing-page exit rate and higher demo click-through for paid search traffic.
hypotheses.expected_business_outcome: More qualified demo requests per paid search dollar, bringing acquisition cost back down.

supporting.claim: Customers repeatedly say they cannot tell what plans include, and these comments are rising; one names arriving from a search ad.
Paid search exits on the pricing page are well above other sources and rising each month, with fewer demo clicks.
Paid search acquisition cost rose sharply as spend grew while wins fell.
Fewer paid search visits become leads than benchmark, consistent with evaluators leaving before converting.

missing: Pricing verbatims are not tagged by acquisition channel, so the paid search link rests on a few mentions.
No pricing-page survey or session recordings show which plan details confuse visitors.

hypotheses.title: A broken mobile demo form loses ready-to-buy visitors
hypotheses.observed_problem: Mobile visitors start the demo form often but rarely finish it, rage-click, and wait on a slow page.
hypotheses.affected_audience: Mobile visitors on the demo page across channels
hypotheses.causal_explanation: A technical defect or slow script on the mobile demo page blocks form submission.
hypotheses.intervention: Profile and fix the mobile demo page and form, then verify completion tracking.
hypotheses.expected_behavior_change: Mobile demo-form completion rises toward the desktop rate.
hypotheses.expected_business_outcome: More demo requests and pipeline without additional spend.

supporting.claim: Mobile demo-form completion is far below desktop, with many more rage clicks and much slower loads.
Prospects report the demo form spinning or freezing on their phones.

missing: We cannot yet tell how many mobile starters later complete the form on desktop.
Server-side demo request counts by device would rule out a tracking gap.

hypotheses.title: Slow partner follow-up loses partner demand
hypotheses.observed_problem: Many partner leads wait longer than a day for first contact.
hypotheses.causal_explanation: Partner leads route to a separate team that responds slowly.
hypotheses.intervention: Route partner leads through the same response-time rules as direct leads.
hypotheses.expected_behavior_change: Faster first contact for partner leads.
hypotheses.expected_business_outcome: Higher partner acceptance and win rates.

supporting.claim: A large share of partner MQLs is contacted after the SLA.

contradicting.claim: Late partner leads are accepted about as often as on-time ones, so delay has no measurable cost yet.

missing: Partner win rates by response time.

action_detail: Change the webinar qualification process: add intent questions to registration, require an intent signal before a webinar contact becomes an MQL, and route the rest to nurture.
guardrail_metric: Webinar-sourced qualified pipeline must not fall.
downstream_metric: Webinar SQL to opportunity, win rate, and revenue.
learning_objective: Learn whether intent screening raises webinar lead quality without shrinking real demand.
missing_evidence: MQL scoring rules and their weights.
Lead-level linkage between customer evidence and funnel records.
